name: ACI Marina Split
fees: €168/night for a boat up to 12 m, 1 Jul–31 Aug 2026 (ACI price list 2026)
approach: Through the busy Split ferry port (ships have right of way, no anchoring); enter close to the head of the inner breakwater (Fl R 2s) east of Sustipan.
notes: Max length 90 m for daily berths (26 m annual); 15 dry berths. Fuel station 0.05 NM away. Old town and Diocletian's Palace a short walk along the Riva.

name: ACI Marina Dubrovnik
fees: €118/night for a boat up to 12 m, 1 Jul–31 Aug 2026 (ACI price list 2026)
approach: From Daksa islet into Rijeka Dubrovačka (170–400 m wide); beyond Rožat the inlet narrows with 3–5 m depth; marina behind a long breakwater, floodlit at night.
notes: 6 km up the inlet from Dubrovnik old town (bus/taxi). 120 dry berths; fuel station listed among marina services.

name: Marina Kornati
approach: Entrance 40 m wide with up to 6.5 m depth, off the Biograd waterfront facing Pašman channel.
notes: Large charter base (300+ charter boats), so Friday/Saturday changeover days are busy. Price list 2026 is a PDF on the marina site.

name: D-Marin Dalmacija
season: all year; water and power 24 h
approach: Call on VHF 17 before entering; transit pier for superyachts up to 70 m.
notes: One of the largest marinas in the Adriatic, 10 km south of Zadar; 300 dry berths, travel lifts 30/35/80 t, fuel station on site.

name: D-Marin Gouvia
season: all year; water and electricity 24 h
approach: Call on VHF 69 before entering Gouvia bay, about 7 km north of Corfu town.
notes: Port of entry hub for the Ionian; 500 dry berths, travel lifts 65 and 75 t.

name: D-Marin Lefkas
season: all year; water and electricity 24 h
approach: Through the Lefkas canal (swing bridge opens on the hour) to the marina on the east shore of the town; call VHF 69. Draft limit 3.3 m.
notes: 280 dry berths; hotel, supermarket and fuel station on site. Lefkas town is next to the marina.

name: D-Marin Zea
season: all year; water and electricity 24 h
approach: Call on VHF 9 before entering for berthing instructions.
notes: Fuel by tanker truck only. Central Piraeus, metro to Athens. D-Marin quotes drafts up to 8 m.

name: D-Marin Göcek
season: all year; office 08:30–18:30 (1 Mar–31 Oct), 08:30–17:00 in winter
approach: Call on VHF 73 on arrival; naturally sheltered deep bay at the head of the Gulf of Fethiye.
notes: 150 dry berths; Dalaman airport about 20 km. Transit log required.

name: D-Marin Valletta
approach: In Marsamxett Harbour at Pietà (Sa Maison), below Valletta's walls; call VHF 13.
notes: Alongside transit berthing for yachts of 50 m and more. Valletta is a short walk.

name: Alimos Marina
approach: Call on VHF 71 well before the entrance and wait to be guided to a berth.
notes: Greece's largest charter base, busiest on Friday–Saturday changeovers; 600 boats in winter dry storage. Berthing application and price list on the marina site.

name: Kos Marina
approach: Entrance at 36°53′N 27°18′E, one mile south-east of Kos old harbour; call VHF 77.
notes: 80 extra berths at Mandraki (old harbour); 150 dry berths. Fridays are busy, at the fuel dock too; book ahead. Town 15 min walk.

name: Marina di Portisco
approach: In the bay of Portisco on the north-east coast of Sardinia, between Olbia and Porto Rotondo; call VHF 69.
notes: Base for cruising the Costa Smeralda and La Maddalena archipelago; Olbia airport about 20 km.

name: Venezia Certosa Marina
approach: From the Lido entrance (Porto di Lido) follow the channel north of Certosa island; access channel about 2.5 m at low water; call VHF 72.
notes: On Certosa island, vaporetto stop at the marina for St Mark's (about 10 min). Book ahead in summer. Depth given is the access channel at low water.

name: Marina di Stabia
approach: At Castellammare di Stabia in the south-east corner of the Bay of Naples, 40°43.03′N 14°28.32′E; call VHF 69.
notes: Gateway to Pompeii, Sorrento and the Amalfi coast. Berth counts differ between sources (789–900).

name: Marina Porto Antico
season: all year; mooring staff 7 days a week
approach: Inside Genoa's commercial port; enter through the main harbour entrance and head for the old port basin by the Aquarium; call VHF 74.
notes: In the heart of Genoa, steps from the historic centre and the Aquarium. Berths 6–75 m.

name: Port Hercule
season: all year; VHF 12 monitored 24 h, reception 07:30–21:30 in season
approach: Enter past the semi-floating outer breakwater; 3-knot speed limit inside. Stern-to with lazy lines.
notes: Fuel at the BP station on the landing stage. Basin depths 2.5 to 55 m. Very limited space during the Grand Prix and Yacht Show; call ahead.

name: Marina Ibiza
approach: In the north part of Ibiza harbour (Eivissa), facing Dalt Vila across the bay.
notes: Fuel station in the marina, with delivery to the berth available. Berths up to 110 m; very expensive and busy in July–August.

name: Port Vauban
fees: about €22/day for an 8 m boat (2026 guide)
approach: Call on VHF 9 to arrange a berth before entering; 3-knot limit inside. Depths 2–8 m depending on basin.
notes: Europe's largest pleasure port by number of berths, beside Antibes old town; superyacht 'IYCA' quay. Berth counts differ between sources (about 1,500–1,700).

name: Port de Nice
fees: €25/day or €175/week for an 8 m boat (bord-de-mer listing)
season: all year; office 07:00–21:00 in season, 08:00–18:00 out of season
approach: Commercial and ferry port: give way to ships, announce every movement on VHF 9 before manoeuvring.
notes: Old town and Castle Hill next to the port. Ask the harbour office which quay berths are free.

name: Port Tino Rossi
approach: Reception pontoon at the foot of the jetty light, outside; fuel berth inside the harbour among the fishing boats. VHF 9 for both Ajaccio ports.
notes: Right below the old town and the citadel. 2-hour free stopover. Port Charles Ornano lies 1.5 km north as an alternative.

name: Port de Bonifacio
season: all year; office 07:30–20:30 from 1 Jun to 30 Sep, 08:30–16:30 out of season
approach: Narrow fjord-like inlet under the cliffs; entrance hard to see from offshore. Pertusato semaphore on VHF 10; strong westerlies in the Bonifacio Strait.
notes: Quai Noël Beretti. Old town on the cliff above. Very crowded in July–August; arrive early.

name: OneOcean Port Vell
approach: Through Barcelona's main harbour entrance and the old port (Port Vell) inner basin, past the swing footbridge at Moll d'Espanya; call VHF 68.
notes: Superyacht-oriented marina in the city centre next to the Barceloneta and the Gothic quarter; smaller boats are better served at Marina Vela or Port Fòrum.

name: Club de Mar Mallorca
approach: West side of Palma bay at Portopí, entered from the main Palma harbour; call VHF 9 for berthing instructions.
notes: More than 70 superyacht berths; depths 3–9 m. Palma cathedral about 3 km along the Paseo Marítimo.

name: Club Marítimo de Mahón
approach: Up the 3-mile natural harbour of Maó; port pilots and traffic on VHF 14, marinas on VHF 9. Moorings along Moll de Llevant below the town.
notes: Other options in the harbour: Marina Port Mahón (superyachts 25–60 m), Marina Menorca and Ports IB moorings (Moll de Llevant/Ponent).

name: Grand Harbour Marina
approach: Keep a listening watch on VHF 12 (Valletta VTS) in Grand Harbour; call the marina on VHF 13 for berthing. Marina along the Birgu (Vittoriosa) waterfront in Dockyard Creek.
notes: 26 superyacht berths; Valletta across the harbour by ferry or water taxi. Operated by Camper & Nicholsons.

name: Netsel Marmaris Marina
approach: In the north-east corner of Marmaris bay by the old town; Setur lists VHF 72, many guides still give VHF 6 ('Port Marmaris').
notes: Port of entry; town-centre location. Depth 3.5–18 m.

name: Milta Bodrum Marina
approach: In Bodrum's western bay below the castle; call VHF 73.
notes: Port of entry in the town centre. Berth counts and draught limits vary between guides (draught 5–7 m quoted).

name: Marina du Château
season: all year; office 08:00–20:00 daily 1 Jun–15 Sep, shorter hours Mon–Sat in winter
approach: Entrance 47 m wide beside the naval base; entry can be stopped by light signals while warships manoeuvre. Phone the day before and call VHF 9 on arrival.
notes: Max draught 4.5 m. Below the château and city centre; Moulin Blanc marina is the other Brest option.

name: Port de La Trinité-sur-Mer
aliases: Port de plaisance de La Trinité-sur-Mer
fees: about €32/day or €224/week for an 8 m boat (2026 guide)
season: all year; office in summer about 08:00–20:00 with night watch
approach: Up the buoyed Crac'h river from Quiberon Bay; visitor pontoon next to the harbour office.
notes: Classic offshore racing port, run by Compagnie des Ports du Morbihan. Visitor berth figures differ (120–150).

name: Cowes Yacht Haven
approach: In the mouth of the River Medina call 'Cowes Yacht Haven' on VHF 80 and follow the dockmaster's instructions (North or South Basin).
notes: Phone or email ahead to pre-book. Fuel at the Cowes Harbour Commission fuel berth or Lallows. Packed during Cowes Week and the Round the Island Race.

name: Lymington Yacht Haven
approach: First marina on the port hand up the Lymington River from the western Solent; call VHF 80 for a berth. Minimum 2.5 m below chart datum, some berths 3 m.
notes: Free water, electricity and wifi at visitor berths. Watch the Isle of Wight ferries in the river.

name: Sixhaven
fees: €24/night for a boat up to 12 m, electricity, water, showers and wifi included (Sixhaven 2025 rates)
season: visitors in the sailing season; maximum stay three weeks
approach: On the north bank of the IJ opposite Centraal Station, next to the Noordhollandsch Kanaal; entrance on the east side behind a steel breakwater. Watch the ferries.
notes: No reservations: phone about five minutes before arrival. Boats over 15 m only by arrangement. Free 24/7 ferries to the centre, 5 min walk.

name: Compagnieshaven
approach: Directly off the IJsselmeer north of Enkhuizen town; no lock needed.
notes: Largest Enkhuizen marina; old town and the Krabbersgat lock to the Markermeer nearby. Capacity figures vary (600–700); draught 2.8–3.2 m quoted.

name: Bataviahaven
fees: municipal tariff table for 2026 (incl. 21% VAT) published by Lelystad
approach: On the Markermeer side of Lelystad by Batavia Stad and the Houtribsluizen (locks to the IJsselmeer).
notes: Next to the Batavia replica ship yard and outlet centre. Municipal harbour run by Lelystad.

name: VYN – Vlaamse Yachthaven Nieuwpoort
season: all year; harbour office 08:30–21:00 on weekdays (ADAC)
approach: Up the IJzer from the Nieuwpoort entrance; tie up temporarily at the head of pontoon B and call VHF 8 for a berth.
notes: One of Europe's largest marina complexes; VVW Westhoek (VHF 77) and Novus Portus are the other Nieuwpoort marinas.

name: Mercator Marina
season: open daily in season (to end October); lock hours by phone
approach: Through the Mercator lock: always call the harbour office on VHF 14 before entering; grouped lockings every half hour, waiting pontoon outside the lock along Churchillkaai. Lock may close at spring tides or in storms.
notes: Lock-protected, no swell, in the centre of Ostend next to the station. New pontoons inaugurated June 2026.

name: Marina Gdańsk
season: harbour master 08:00–19:00 (ADAC); marina accessible day and night
approach: From Gdańsk Bay via the Martwa Wisła and the Motława river to the old town; the marina is on the east bank (Szafarnia) opposite the Długie Pobrzeże.
notes: Run by Gdański Ośrodek Sportu, which also operates Sienna Grobla, Tamka, Nadwiślańska, Górki Zachodnie and Żabi Kruk. Old town and the Crane steps away. Max draught 3.5–4 m quoted.

name: Wasahamnen
fees: SEK 400/night for boats up to 12 m (SEK 700 over 12 m, SEK 1,100 over 20 m) plus SEK 150 electricity, summer season 15 May–15 Sep (2026 price list)
season: all year; office 08:00–20:00 daily 15 May–15 Sep; water and power off 15 Nov–1 Apr
approach: On Djurgården opposite Gamla stan, by the Vasa Museum. Boats over 13.5 m or multihulls over 4 m beam go to the outside of pier D (max 20 m). Mooring on buoys at pier A.
notes: Guest harbour only; 26 of the 126 places are bookable via Dockspot. Basin depth at least 2.5 m at mean water. No rafting up.

name: Langelinie Lystbådehavn
season: guest facilities close for winter from 1 November
approach: North of the city centre at Langelinie, by the Little Mermaid, entered from the main Copenhagen harbour fairway.
notes: Walk to Nyhavn and Amalienborg. Guest stays in Copenhagen harbour limited to one month per season.

name: Göteborgs Gästhamn Lilla Bommen
season: open 24 h all year; full service 1 May–30 Sep
approach: Up the Göta älv from the sea, past the Älvsborg bridge, to the city centre by the Opera house.
notes: Short walk to Nordstan and Central Station. Start of the Göta älv route to Trollhätte canal and Lake Vänern.

name: HSS Guest Marina Liuskasaari
fees: €40/day or €200/week (HSS guest marina price list)
season: summer season; harbour masters about 08:00–16:00 Mon–Fri
approach: Liuskasaari island off Kaivopuisto, south of the city centre; guest berths E1–E23 on buoys at the south-west end of the northernmost concrete pier, depth 3–4 m.
notes: Club ferry to the mainland included; Market Square within walking distance. Book and pay via satamapaikka.com.

name: Old City Marina
season: marina office 08:00–20:00 in season; Port Control 24/7
approach: Inside Tallinn's Old City Harbour (ferry port): ask permission to enter from Port Control on VHF 14 ('Tallinn Radio 5') or by phone +372 631 8588.
notes: Floating berths for boats up to 18 m, draught 4.0 m; quays 18–23 take up to 50 m. Old town 10 min walk. Run by Port of Tallinn.

name: Marina Lanke
fees: €48/day for a boat up to 12 m plus €5 per adult per day (water, power, showers included), price list valid from 3 Jun 2026
approach: On the Scharfe Lanke bay off the Havel in Spandau, west Berlin; about 30 min to the city centre.
notes: Largest marina in Berlin; no houseboats accepted. Boat fuel station (Bootstankstelle Berlin) on site, also for masted yachts. Pump-out €30 per use.

name: Port de l'Arsenal
season: all year; office 08:00–20:00 in July–August 2026, 09:00–20:00 in September
approach: From the Seine (PK 168) through the Arsenal lock (air draught 5.20 m, draught 1.90 m); call on VHF 9. An older city document says lock requests are on VHF 20, so check with the harbour office.
notes: Between the Seine and Place de la Bastille, start of the Canal Saint-Martin. Book well ahead in summer.

name: Port de Plaisance de Strasbourg
aliases: Club du Port de Plaisance de Strasbourg
approach: In the Port Autonome de Strasbourg off the Rhine; the Strasbourg Rhine locks work on VHF 22 (+33 3 88 39 12 61). VNF vignette required on French waterways.
notes: Other moorings in town: Port EVAE (rue de Prague, near the centre), Marinest, Plaisance Club de Strasbourg. Contact the operator before arrival.

name: Halte fluviale de la Confluence
approach: In the Place Nautique basin off the Saône at Quai Rambaud, just above the Saône–Rhône confluence.
notes: Berths for boats of 20 m and 28 m; around 500 visiting boats a season, average stay two days. Shopping centre and tram next to the basin.

name: Wiking Marina Budapest
approach: On the Danube at Hajógyári-sziget (Óbuda island), Buda side, north of the city centre.
notes: Wiking Yacht Club base with crane, workshop and fuel station; its smaller Marina Part (80 berths on floating jetties) is about 1 km north. Details from a 2012 report; confirm with the club.

name: Marina Wien
fees: €81/day for a boat of 12 m (€494/week), guest price list valid from 1 Apr 2026; over 12 m and catamarans on request
approach: On the right bank of the Danube at river km 1926.1, Handelskai in Leopoldstadt; U2 station 'Donaumarina'.
notes: Two basins, fenced and CCTV-guarded. Fuel station with diesel and petrol 95. Underground to the centre in minutes.

name: Ekomarina Giżycko
fees: PLN 60/day for boats under 9 m, PLN 80 for 9–12 m (city tariff, Zarządzenie 1396/2024)
approach: On Lake Niegocin at the town centre of Giżycko, by the Łuczański canal.
notes: Municipal marina at ul. Dąbrowskiego 14, main hub of the Great Masurian Lakes. Max draught 1.5 m (ADAC).

name: Wioska Żeglarska Mikołajki
approach: Town centre of Mikołajki on the north shore of Jezioro Mikołajskie, south of the road bridge.
notes: About 150 yachts a day in season (third-party figure). Busy in July–August; the Ekomarina MKŻ and other quays nearby.

name: Port d'Ouchy
fees: CHF 20 + VAT per night, CHF 40 + VAT from the 11th night (City of Lausanne, 2026)
season: Bureau du lac Mon–Fri 07:30–11:30 and 13:00–17:00; visitor berths closed on some event dates in summer
approach: Lake Geneva harbour entrance 6 m wide with 2.50 m height limit; watch for CGN ferries.
notes: 8 visitor berths on the north quay plus 14 orange buoys in the old port; no reservations. Moor at a free visitor berth and register with the Bureau du lac (at Port de Vidy, which has 22 more).

name: North East Marina
approach: On Grodzka island in the Odra (Odra Zachodnia) opposite Szczecin old town and the Wały Chrobrego; reached from the Szczecin Lagoon via the Odra.
notes: Floating pontoons; old town over the bridge. Marina Goclaw is a second Szczecin option.

name: Liberty Landing Marina
fees: about $6/ft/night under 65 ft (Waterway Guide, 2022 rates; likely higher now)
approach: Morris Canal basin on the Jersey City side of the Hudson opposite lower Manhattan; call on VHF 72 for a slip.
notes: The usual Great Loop base for New York City: ferry to Manhattan from the marina. Bookings through Molo.

name: Waterford Harbor Visitor Center
aliases: Richard M. Hurst Harbor Visitors Center
fees: free wall/floating dock up to 48 h; about $10/day for power (boater reviews 2023–2025)
approach: At the junction of the Hudson and the Erie Canal, just below Erie Lock E2 of the Waterford Flight.
notes: First come, first served; the floating dock fills early in summer. Gateway to the Erie and Champlain canals.

name: Wright's Landing Marina
fees: $2.00/ft/day with power, $1.50 without (City of Oswego)
approach: Inside the Oswego harbour breakwaters on Lake Ontario, west of the Oswego River mouth.
notes: City marina at the Lake Ontario end of the Oswego Canal.

name: Confederation Basin Marina
fees: CAD 2.26/ft/day unserviced, 2.61 serviced in July–Aug; 2.08/2.26 May, June, Sep, Oct; power extra (city rates)
approach: Downtown in front of City Hall behind the Shoal Tower; call VHF 68 for your slip on arrival.
notes: Fuel and pump-out are at Portsmouth Olympic Harbour, west of downtown. Southern end of the Rideau Canal.

name: Trent Port Marina
fees: about CAD 2.32/ft/day (Waterway Guide listing)
approach: At the mouth of the Trent River on the Bay of Quinte; the fuel dock is just upriver (north) of the marina.
notes: Southern entrance to the Trent–Severn Waterway (Lock 1 is a short way upriver).

name: Lock 45 – Port Severn
fees: Parks Canada overnight mooring permit, charged per foot
approach: Smallest lock on the waterway (25.6 × 7.0 m), which limits boat size for the whole route; currents below the lock in high water, narrow channel under Highway 400.
notes: Northern (Georgian Bay) end of the Trent–Severn. Overnight mooring max 2 nights. Marinas with fuel, e.g. Starport Marina, are just above the lock.

name: Mackinac Island State Harbor
approach: Harbor in front of the town, protected by a breakwater; hail on VHF 9.
notes: Very busy; booking limited mid-June to late July (Chicago/Port Huron races). Max 4 consecutive nights at busy times. Off-season phone +1 906-643-8620.

name: DuSable Harbor
season: 1 May – 31 Oct (office hours vary through the season)
approach: Inside the Chicago outer harbor breakwater just north of the Chicago River entrance; transient slips are on floating docks.
notes: Downtown harbor at the start of the Chicago River route to the Illinois Waterway. Reservations via Dockwa from 1 May.

name: Grafton Harbor
approach: Floating docks at the confluence of the Illinois and Mississippi rivers.
notes: Diesel availability has been patchy after floods in past years; call ahead before relying on it.

name: Paducah Transient Boat Dock
fees: $1.75/ft/night from 1 May 2026 incl. power (half rate without power/water), plus 6% tax (city rules)
season: seasonal; amenities disconnected when the river nears 39 ft
approach: Ohio River mile 935 downtown; approach perpendicular to the channel because of a downstream shoal.
notes: Nine power/water pedestals. Fuel not staffed: call on approach; boats after 2 pm are fuelled next day. Office 8:30–16:00.

name: Green Turtle Bay Resort & Marina
approach: On Lake Barkley near the Barkley Canal to Kentucky Lake; fuel dock in front of the office, transient slips mostly west of it.
notes: Classic Great Loop stop between the Cumberland/Tennessee rivers; non-ethanol petrol.

name: Kingfisher Bay Marina
approach: Basin off the Tombigbee at Demopolis; check in at the Yacht Basin fuel dock.
notes: Main fuel and boatyard stop on the Tenn-Tom; Quimby's lists marine diesel and 89-octane non-ethanol petrol.

name: Dog River Marina
approach: Up Dog River off the west side of Mobile Bay; 8 ft minimum approach.
notes: Main transient and repair stop for Mobile at the bottom of the Tenn-Tom. Fuel dock phone +1 251-471-4517.

name: Scipio Creek Marina
fees: $3/ft/day (Waterway Guide, 2023)
approach: Off the Apalachicola River at the north end of town.
notes: Long face docks rather than slips, boats tied end to end; call ahead.

name: Tarpon Springs City Marina
aliases: City of Tarpon Springs Municipal Marina
fees: $1.50/ft/night (Soundings; date unknown)
approach: Up the Anclote River to the historic sponge docks on Dodecanese Blvd; floating docks.
notes: Only a handful of transient slips; reserve. Sponge Docks restaurants alongside.

name: Legacy Harbour Marina
approach: Downtown Fort Myers on the Caloosahatchee (Okeechobee Waterway); 7 ft approach, soft mud.
notes: Floating docks; western end of the Okeechobee Waterway.

name: Sunset Bay Marina & Anchorage
approach: St. Lucie River at mile 8 of the Okeechobee Waterway, downtown Stuart.
notes: Also 69 moorings. Eastern end of the Okeechobee Waterway; book directly (not via Dockwa).

name: Miami Beach Marina
approach: Just inside Government Cut at the south end of Miami Beach, off Alton Road.
notes: Closest marina to the ocean inlet; South Beach on foot.

name: Las Olas Marina
approach: On the ICW by the Las Olas Blvd bridge, Fort Lauderdale beach.
notes: Site under redevelopment (2024–26 reviews); nearby city mooring field (about $35/night, no reservations) is city-managed.

name: Safe Harbor Charleston City
approach: Ashley River side of the peninsula; transients mostly on the long Megadock; fuel hoses reach its end.
notes: Shuttle to the historic district.

name: Beaufort Town Docks
approach: Taylor's Creek off Front Street: via Gallants Channel under the 65 ft bridge, or Bulkhead Channel from Beaufort Inlet.
notes: Fuel delivered at the slip. ICW mile 202; loaner cars.

name: Tidewater Yacht Marina
approach: Elizabeth River opposite downtown Norfolk, near ICW mile 0.
notes: Reviews in 2026 report the diesel pumps out of service: call before counting on fuel.

name: Annapolis City Dock
fees: $3/ft Sun–Thu, $4/ft Fri–Sat and holidays (city page, Jan 2026); city moorings about $35/night
approach: Head of Ego Alley off Spa Creek; city mooring fields in Spa Creek and the harbor.
notes: City Dock resiliency works 2026–early 2028 close many slips; limited bulkhead in Ego Alley. Pump-out boat Wed–Sun via VHF 17.

name: Port d'escale du Vieux-Port de Montréal
fees: CAD 4.00/ft/night (25–59 ft), 4.50 in high season and weekends, 5.00 on event dates (2026, before tax)
approach: Old Port basin off the St. Lawrence; Ste-Marie current up to 6 kn outside, 10 km/h limit inside.
notes: Fuelling only with supervisor authorization. Booking by request form; 2027 bookings open in April.

name: Ottawa Locks (Rideau Canal)
fees: CAD 1.50/ft overnight; power CAD 12/night where available (2026)
approach: Flight of 8 locks between the Ottawa River and the canal beside Parliament Hill; arrive at least 3.5 h before closing to lock through.
notes: Max 2 nights; first come, first served, check in with lock staff. Power on the wall reported by boaters but not confirmed.

name: Marina du Port de Québec
fees: CAD 3.30/ft/night up to 59 ft, 3.90 for 60–79 ft (2026)
approach: Bassin Louise beside Old Québec, entered through a lock from the St. Lawrence; large tides, check lock times.
notes: Fuel at the service dock 8:00–20:00 daily.

name: Burlington Community Boathouse
approach: Behind the Burlington breakwater on Lake Champlain, foot of College Street.
notes: Also about 51 transient moorings by the breakwall. Fuel at Burlington Harbor Marina nearby.

name: Bell Harbor Marina
fees: guest rate from about $2.64/ft/day under 50 ft (Port of Seattle page 2026; 20 ft minimum)
approach: On the downtown Elliott Bay waterfront at Pier 66, inside a breakwater.
notes: Port of Seattle guest-only marina downtown; reservations recommended.

name: Cap Sante Marina
fees: call for rates (WPPA guide 2026)
season: all year; fuel dock 8:00–18:00 summer, 8:00–16:30 winter
approach: Fidalgo Bay side of Anacortes; call VHF 66A for a slip.
notes: US Customs port of entry: call +1 360-293-2331 an hour before arrival. Gateway to the San Juans.

name: Causeway Marina (Victoria Inner Harbour)
fees: CAD 3.02/ft/night for 30–45 ft in summer (22 Jun – 21 Sep), 2.29 low season; power extra (GVHA 2026)
approach: Inner Harbour has mandatory traffic lanes and floatplanes; clear CBSA at the Raymur Point customs dock, then hail GVHA on 66A.
notes: Causeway floats in front of the Empress take boats to 60 ft; larger boats at Ship Point/Wharf Street.

name: Coal Harbour Marina
approach: Coal Harbour, inside Burrard Inlet past Brockton Point, downtown Vancouver.
notes: Guest moorage to 330 ft; reservations highly recommended. Fuel from the fuel barge in Coal Harbour.

name: Nanaimo Boat Basin
approach: Downtown behind the concrete breakwater; hail the wharfinger on VHF 67 for a berth.
notes: Customs clearing area on the north side of E float. Inner basin gates locked 23:00–07:00.

name: Thomas Basin
approach: Small basin at the south end of downtown, just past the cruise ship docks.
notes: Transient moorage in all city harbors; register at the harbormaster office at Bar Harbor and prepay open-moorage permits.
sources: https://www.ketchikan.gov/media/Port & Harbors/Harbor/Welcome To Ketchikan Harbors Booklet.pdf

name: Harris Harbor
fees: $0.75/ft/day from 1 Jul 2025 (CBJ rate chart FY26)
approach: Walking distance north of downtown; pass under the Douglas Bridge (about 20 m clearance). Hail Aurora Harbor Office on VHF 73 entering Gastineau Channel.
notes: Transient space first come, first served through the Aurora Harbor Office; Aurora Harbor (365 slips) just north.

name: Shelter Island Guest Docks
fees: $1.27/ft/day (Port of San Diego; year not stated)
approach: Shelter Island Yacht Basin at the Harbor Police station.
